title: Routing grammar circuit-breaker rewrite and staged schema safety checks
creator: Sarah Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's routing configuration DSL has accumulated ad-hoc conditionals and implicit fallbacks which make it hard to reason about region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. This has led to subtle production incidents where capacity constraints or tiered fallbacks were mis-evaluated and requests routed to suboptimal variants, causing increased latency and cost for customers.

Problem statement:
- The current parser accepts overlapping constructs that allow ambiguous precedence between region selectors, tier weights, and fallback variants.
- There is no lightweight circuit-breaker concept for policies: a single malformed rule can make the entire route evaluation pessimistic or optimistic in the wrong way.
- Runtime validators only surface errors at runtime in some Dedicated/Private deployments; we need a staged validation path that rejects or warns earlier.

Goal:
Refactor the policy engine's ingest pipeline to introduce an explicit grammar rewrite pass that: 1) canonicalizes precedence for region/tier/fallback clauses; 2) inserts a declarative circuit-breaker node for guarded rules; 3) performs staged schema validation (soft warnings for deprecated constructs, hard errors for unsafe patterns) before publishing to the policy store. The end state should reduce ambiguous routing behavior, improve operator visibility, and enable safe automated migrations for existing rules.

Proposed approach:
1) Grammar & AST changes:
   - Introduce a canonical AST node type "guarded_block" that wraps vulnerable constructs and includes failover semantics and metrics tags.
   - Define explicit precedence: region selection -> tier resolution -> variant fallback. Create rewrite rules to transform legacy shapes (eg. combined "region:tier" inline clauses) into the canonical AST.
   - Add a small, well-documented EBNF appendix for the new sanitized DSL surface.

2) Circuit-breaker semantics:
   - A circuit-breaker is an attribute on policy blocks: "cb: {threshold_ms, error_rate_pct, window_s}". If tripped, evaluation will immediately route to the declared fallback variant or the global fallback chain.
   - Default circuit-breaker for any block without explicit cb will be conservative: threshold_ms=10000, error_rate_pct=20, window_s=60.

3) Staged validation pipeline:
   - Stage 0 (lint): best-effort autofix suggestions and deprecation warnings. Non-blocking.
   - Stage 1 (soft validate): critical suspicious patterns flagged, require explicit opt-in to allow for automated migration. Emits dashboard events and comments on policy diff PRs.
   - Stage 2 (hard validate): structural errors that prevent policy from being published to the active store. Runs in CI for private/dedicated deployments and as preflight for hosted policy pushes.

4) Migration strategy:
   - A migration CLI mode that runs existing policies through the rewrite pass and produces a side-by-side diff with suggested guarded_block insertions and recommended cb params.
   - Rollout: start with internal Canary orgs -> opt-in set of tenants -> global enforcement after 6 weeks of monitoring.

Acceptance criteria:
- New parser emits canonical AST for >99% of existing policy shapes and provides a clear error for ambiguous constructs.
- Staged validator implemented and wired to the policy publishing flow; Stage 0/1 warnings visible in Console policy diffs.
- Circuit-breaker nodes added to transformed policies using default params where not specified.
- Migration CLI created (policy-rewrite --dry-run) and validated against a sample of 2000 real policies from the policy store without data loss.
- Performance: parse+rewrite latency < 50ms p95 for policies up to 2KB.
- Automated tests and property-based fuzzing added to prevent regressions.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for grammar rewrite rules with canonicalization snapshot testing.
- Integration tests for staged validation pipeline including simulated publishing flow.
- Canary runtime tests: deploy to a dedicated canary cluster and measure routing outcomes against golden queries for region/tier/fallback scenarios.
- Chaos test: intentionally trip circuit-breaker thresholds to validate fallback routing and observability.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge implementation behind a feature flag (policy-rewrite-v2).
2) Run migration CLI in dry-run across prod policy store to collect diffs and review with policy owners.
3) Enable Stage 0 warnings in Console for all orgs.
4) After 3 weeks, enable Stage 1 soft validate for a subset of high-traffic tenants.
5) After 6 weeks and no critical regressions, flip the feature flag to enable hard validate on publish for all hosted orgs; provide a 14-day grace period for Dedicated/Private customers, with support-runbook.

Out-of-scope:
- Changes to backend runtime evaluation optimizations (this ticket focuses on control-plane grammar/validation only).
- UI redesign of Console diffs beyond adding the new warning/error markers.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Overaggressive rewrites could change routing semantics. Mitigation: keep a conservative default policy for cb and require explicit opt-in to any semantic-changing hard validate. Maintain a full audit log of original policy and rewritten policy.
- Risk: Performance regressions in the policy publish pipeline. Mitigation: run benchmarks; ensure rewrite happens asynchronously where appropriate and limit synchronous checks to Stage 2 only.
